original_text:
Inflation Expectations Stable; Labor Market Expectations Mixed
November 09, 2026

NEW YORK—The  Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s Center for Microeconomic Data today released  the October 2026
Survey of Consumer Expectations
, which shows that  households’ inflation expectations remained unchanged at the short-, medium-,  and longer-term horizons. Labor market expectations were mixed with  unemployment and job loss expectations deteriorating, while job finding expectations  improved.  Expectations  of an increase in unemployment reached the highest level since April 2020.  Conversely, job finding expectations reached their highest level since November  2025. Income and spending growth expectations were broadly stable while  delinquency expectations deteriorated. The survey was fielded from October 1  through October 31, 2026.
The main findings from the October 2026Survey  are:
Inflation
Median inflation expectations were unchanged at the one-year, three-year, and  five-year-ahead horizons at 3.9%, 3.3%, and 3.0%, respectively. The survey’s  measure of disagreement across respondents (the difference between the 75th and  25th percentiles of inflation expectations) decreased at the one-year and  five-year horizons and remained unchanged at the three-year-ahead horizon.
Median inflation uncertainty—or the  uncertainty expressed regarding future inflation outcomes—decreased at the one-  and three-year horizons and was unchanged at the five-year horizon.
Median home price  growth expectations were unchanged at 3.0%, just below its 12-month trailing  average of 3.1%.
Among  commodities, median year-ahead expected price changes decreased by 0.6  percentage point to 4.2% for gas and were unchanged at 5.5% for food. Median  year-ahead expected price changes increased by 0.1 percentage point to 9.3% for  the cost of medical care, by 0.1 percentage point to 7.6% for the cost of  college education, and by 0.9 percentage point to 7.7% for rent.
Labor Market
Median one-year-ahead earnings  growth expectations remained unchanged at 2.6% in October. The series remains just  below its 12-month trailing average of 2.7%.
Mean unemployment expectations—or  the mean probability that the U.S. unemployment rate will be higher one year  from now—increased by 1.4 percentage points to 45.3%, its highest reading since  April 2020. The increase was driven by those without a college degree.
The mean perceived probability of  losing one’s job in the next 12 months increased by 0.4 percentage point to 13.9%,  remaining below its 12-month trailing average of 14.3%. The mean probability of  leaving one’s job voluntarily, or  the expected quit rate, in the next 12 months decreased by 0.5 percentage point  to 19.4%, remaining above the series’ 12-month trailing average of 18.4%.
The mean perceived probability of  finding a job if one’s current job was lost increased by 0.4 percentage point  to 46.5%, its highest level since November 2025.
Household Finance
The  median expected growth in household income declined by 0.1 percentage point to 3.0% in October. The  series has been moving in a narrow range between 2.8% and 3.1% since June 2025.
Median  one-year-ahead household spending  growth expectations decreased by 0.2 percentage point to 5.3%, remaining above its 12-month trailing average of 5.0%.
Perceptions  of credit access compared to a year ago and expectations for future credit availability were roughly unchanged.
The average perceived probability of missing a  minimum debt payment over the next three months increased  by 1.6 percentage points to 13.8%>, its highest level since December 2025.
The  median expectation regarding a year-ahead change in taxes at one’s current  income level increased by 0.1 percentage point to 3.8%, its highest reading  since December 2025.
Median  year-ahead expected growth in government debt decreased by 0.2 percentage point  to 9.7%, remaining above its 12-month trailing average of 9.3%.
The  mean perceived probability that the average interest rate on saving accounts  will be higher in 12 months increased by 1.3 percentage points to 31.6%, its  highest level since April 2023.
Perceptions of  households’ financial situations  improved slightly  with the net share of respondents reporting a better financial situation compared  to a year ago increasing. Expectations about households’ financial situation a  year from now were roughly unchanged.
The  mean perceived probability that U.S. stock prices will be higher 12 months from  now decreased by 0.2 percentage point to 40.0%.
About  the Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE)
The SCE contains information about how consumers expect overall  inflation and prices for food, gas, housing, and education to behave. It also  provides insight into Americans’ views about job prospects and earnings growth  and their expectations about future spending and access to credit. The SCE also  provides measures of uncertainty regarding consumers’ outlooks. Expectations  are also available by age, geography, income, education, and numeracy.
The SCE is a nationally representative, internet-based survey of a rotating panel of  approximately 1,300 household heads. Respondents participate in the panel for  up to 12 months, with a roughly equal number rotating in and out of the panel  each month. Unlike comparable surveys based on repeated cross-sections with a  different set of respondents in each wave, this panel allows us to observe the  changes in expectations and behavior of the same individuals over time. For  further information on the SCE, please refer to an overview of the survey  methodology
here
,  the
FAQs
, the
interactive  chart guide
, and the survey
questionnaire

translation_ja:
本稿はNY連銀の2026年11月9日付公表本文の日本語訳です。翻訳は調査側によるものです。

ニューヨーク連銀のミクロ経済データセンターは、2026年10月の消費者期待調査を公表した。家計の短期・中期・長期のインフレ期待は横ばいだった。労働市場では、失業率の上昇や失職への懸念が強まる一方、再就職への期待は改善した。失業率上昇を見込む度合いは2020年4月以来、再就職への期待は2025年11月以来の高水準となった。所得・支出の伸びの期待はおおむね安定したが、延滞の見通しは悪化した。調査期間は2026年10月1～31日。

### インフレ

- 1年・3年・5年先のインフレ期待の中央値は、それぞれ3.9％、3.3％、3.0％で横ばい。回答者間のばらつき（第75百分位と第25百分位の差）は1年・5年先で縮小し、3年先では横ばい。
- 将来のインフレに対する不確実性の中央値は、1年・3年先で低下し、5年先で横ばい。
- 住宅価格上昇期待の中央値は3.0％で横ばい。過去12カ月平均の3.1％をわずかに下回る。
- 1年先の価格変化予想の中央値は、ガソリンが0.6ポイント低下して4.2％、食料は5.5％で横ばい。医療費は0.1ポイント上昇の9.3％、大学教育費は0.1ポイント上昇の7.6％、家賃は0.9ポイント上昇の7.7％。

### 労働市場

- 1年先の勤労所得の伸びの中央値は2.6％で横ばい。過去12カ月平均は2.7％。
- 1年後に米国の失業率が現在より高くなると回答者が考える確率の平均は、1.4ポイント上昇して45.3％となり、2020年4月以来の高水準。上昇は大学学位を持たない層が主導。
- 今後12カ月に失職すると考える確率の平均は0.4ポイント上昇の13.9％で、過去12カ月平均の14.3％を下回る。自発的に離職すると考える確率の平均は0.5ポイント低下の19.4％で、同平均の18.4％を上回る。
- 現職を失った場合に仕事が見つかると考える確率の平均は0.4ポイント上昇して46.5％。2025年11月以来の高水準。

### 家計金融

- 家計所得の伸びの中央値は0.1ポイント低下の3.0％。2025年6月以降は2.8～3.1％の範囲。
- 1年先の家計支出の伸びの中央値は0.2ポイント低下の5.3％。過去12カ月平均の5.0％を上回る。
- 1年前と比べた信用へのアクセスの認識と、今後の信用供与の見通しはおおむね横ばい。
- 今後3カ月に最低返済額を支払えないと考える確率の平均は1.6ポイント上昇の13.8％で、2025年12月以来の高水準。
- 現在の所得水準を前提とした1年先の税額の変化予想の中央値は0.1ポイント上昇の3.8％で、2025年12月以来の高水準。
- 1年先の政府債務の伸びの中央値は0.2ポイント低下の9.7％。過去12カ月平均の9.3％を上回る。
- 12カ月後の平均預金金利が現在より高いと考える確率の平均は1.3ポイント上昇の31.6％で、2023年4月以来の高水準。
- 家計の現在の財政状態に対する認識はやや改善し、1年前より良いと答えた割合のネット値が上昇。1年先の見通しはおおむね横ばい。
- 12カ月後の米株価が現在より高いと考える確率の平均は0.2ポイント低下の40.0％。

### 調査方法

この調査は、全体のインフレや食料・ガソリン・住宅・教育の価格、雇用・所得、支出・信用へのアクセスに関する家計の見通しと不確実性を把握する。年齢、地域、所得、教育、数的能力ごとの結果も利用できる。全米を代表する約1,300世帯の世帯主を対象としたオンラインの交代制パネルで、各回答者は最長12カ月参加し、毎月ほぼ同数が入れ替わる。毎回異なる対象を抽出する横断調査と比べ、同じ回答者の期待や行動の変化を追える。調査方法、よくある質問、図表ガイド、質問票は原文リンクを参照。

title_en: Inflation Expectations Stable; Labor Market Expectations Mixed
title_ja: NY連銀の10月消費者期待調査
publication_time_note: 公表本文は日付を表示。NY連銀公式日程の公表予定は11月9日11:00 EST、実公表時刻は未確認。
facts_ja: 10月の1年・3年・5年先のインフレ期待中央値は3.9％、3.3％、3.0％で横ばい。
1年後の失業率上昇を見込む回答者の平均確率は1.4ポイント上昇して45.3％、2020年4月以来の高水準。失職時の再就職期待は0.4ポイント上昇して46.5％。
今後3カ月の最低返済額の不払い見通しは1.6ポイント上昇して13.8％。いずれも調査回答で、実際の失業率や延滞率とは測定対象が異なる。
inference_ja: インフレ期待が横ばいで雇用不安が増すなら、実際の雇用・消費が弱まる場合に需要減速が政策見通しへ波及し得る。再就職期待の改善は一方向の解釈を弱める。

summary_ja_40: 米ＮＹ連銀の十月調査、物価予想は横ばいで失業率上昇を見込む平均確率は四五・三％。
